subject: Finly — Discovery recap: p95 latency, streaming UX, concurrency requirements
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finly.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@finly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-08T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: Finly — Discovery recap: p95 latency, streaming UX, concurrency requirements

Hi Samir / Lena —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap so we’re all aligned and to confirm next steps.

Pain points we heard
- UI feels sluggish when agents respond; customers expect token-by-token streaming for short answers (chat/assistant flows).
- Current infra hits 600ms+ p95 on short responses which degrades perceived latency for interactive flows.
- Under peak load the system backs up — you see request queueing and tail latency spikes during batch jobs.

Current stack (as described)
- Inference: self-hosted transformer models behind a k8s autoscaling layer (NVIDIA A100 nodes).
- Orchestration: custom request broker + Redis for queues; no prefix/KV cache today.
- Frontend: streaming-enabled React UI expecting token deltas.

Success criteria (what Finly wants from a POC)
- p95 end-to-end latency for short responses (<= 150 ms) in the interactive UI for ~50 token responses.
- Smooth streaming UX (token-by-token / low jitter) for baseline traffic profile.
- Sustain concurrent active sessions: ~500 active users (baseline) with spike capacity to ~2k concurrent.
- No regression in output quality vs. current model (we’ll define evaluation prompts).

Immediate next steps
1) I attached a short POC requirements doc with the data points you promised (traffic profile, model sizes, exact prompt shapes). Please attach network diag if you have it.
2) We’ll scope a 3-week POC: baseline perf runs, streaming integration, and a small-scale production-like run.
3) Marissa / Aditya will follow up with a POC plan + capacity/cost estimate by EOD Monday (Nov 9).

Open questions for Finly
- Can you confirm typical response length distribution (tokens) and the split between short (<=50t) and long responses (>200t)?
- Any regulatory constraints we should be aware of for logging/retention?
- Do you have a preferred time window for the production-like run?

Attachments: finly-poc-requirements.pdf (incl. traffic profile), network_diag.png (optional)

If that looks right I’ll kick off the internal POC planning and loop in infra to reserve capacity.

Thanks,
Dylan
Sr. Account Exec | Redwood Inference
(d) 415-555-0123 | dylan.brooks@redwood.ai

On the call: Samir (Finly, Head of MLInfra), Lena (Finly, Product), Marissa (Redwood Solutions), Aditya (Redwood Performance)

Subject: Re: Finly — Discovery recap: p95 latency, streaming UX, concurrency requirements

Dylan —

Thanks for the clear recap, that aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications:
- The 150 ms p95 target is for UI-perceived latency for short answers (~20-50 tokens). End-to-end includes network + model.
- Our current peak is closer to 1.8k concurrent active sessions (not just background QPS); baseline is ~450.
- We don’t have a hard logging retention policy yet but we need to scope for SOC-related exports down the road.

POC timeline: 3 weeks sounds reasonable. We can provide a traffic dump and the small set of evaluation prompts by tomorrow.

Questions for Redwood:
- For streaming UX, does your runtime support continuous low-latency token streaming with minimal jitter?
- What model sizes/quantization profiles would you recommend for the POC (we currently run a 13B and a 70B variant)?
- Can you share a rough cost ballpark for the 3-week POC (compute + reserved capacity)?

I’ve attached the network diag we talked about.

Samir
Head of ML Infrastructure | Finly
samir@finly.com

Dylan / Marissa —

Quick notes from infra side (will expand into the POC doc):
- Model recommendation: start with 13B quantized to int4 for the interactive flow; keep 70B as fallback for long-form generation. We’ll include kernel/compile settings.
- Runtime features: enable prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts; continuous batching with max batch delay tuned to keep p95 under 150ms for <=50 token responses.
- Streaming: use our streaming connector that pushes deltas; we’ll instrument jitter metrics and a small client-side buffer to smooth UI.
- Capacity plan: reserve a small Dedicated pool for the 3-week POC (N=4 A100-equivalent GPUs) with burst to cloud for the 1-hour soak at 1.8k. Cost ballpark in attached spreadsheet (redwood-poc-estimate.xlsx).

I’ll convert this to the one-page POC plan and share by EOD.

Adi
